correctness.rationale: A point fixed by sigma in the simplicial realization has weights constant on vertex orbits, so the admissible arrow-orbit barycenters triangulate the actual fixed set. An equivariant arrow orbit from source cycle i to target j exists exactly when len(j)|len(i), with len(j) target choices; within-cycle arrows form forbidden directed cycles. A quotient directed cycle lifts to one after repeating a composite shift, giving an exact forest model. Reversing arrows under the divisor-rooted condition supplies a complete source for the weighted quotient forest digraph; the Kozlov/Jojić complete-source shellability theorem applies, and restoring independent phase labels is a positive-integer simplicial expansion that preserves shellability (Moradi–Khosh-Ahang Theorem 2.12). The all-forest matrix determinant is block triangular by divisor lengths, giving stated Q_sigma. Purity plus shellability gives integral wedge type and B_sigma from reduced Euler. The c=1 empty and S^0 conventions were checked. Independently enumerated fixed quotient forest f-polynomials for cycle types (2,4,6), (2,4,8), (2,2,2,4), yielding B=1,5,125 in dimensions 1,1,2, but they are not used to infer arbitrary parameters.

value.rationale: A complete integral homotopy type for geometric fixed-point spaces of a canonical complex under a natural infinite family of cyclic vertex actions, including incomparable divisor lengths. The shellability result is a topological strengthening of a previously known Euler character and explains a structural arithmetic boundary; it is not merely a repetition of the face polynomial.

final_claim: For sigma in S_n acting by relabeling on the ordinary Chari–Joswig graph discrete-Morse complex of K_n, with c cycles and one occurring cycle length dividing every other, the geometric cyclic fixed space is empty if c=1, otherwise has a pure shellable triangulation of dimension c-2, and is a wedge of B=|prod_d (1-S_d)(1-S_d-d m_d)^(m_d-1)| spheres S^(c-2), with face polynomial prod_d (1+S_d z)(1+(S_d+d m_d) z)^(m_d-1).
limitations: No classification for general non-divisor-rooted types or subgroup intersections.
